correctness.rationale: The six autocorrelation representatives and their negatives exhaust the nonzero differences. Squaring and summing with Haar probability gives equation (1); each two-term modulus is majorized by its phase-aligned value. At S=1 the magnitude expression is 1+2[A(s+2q+2t)+q²+t²+xy+4qt]. Replacing q,t by their AM–GM upper bounds x/2,y/2 produces exactly twice the bracket with h,v, which is nonnegative including at zeros. Then xy=(s²−(x−y)²)/4 and completing the square yield coefficients 11/4 and 3/4 and the sharp ratio 27/11. Vanishing of the squares fixes s=8/11, x=y=4/11 and A=3/11; the bracket then forces four equal nonzero arm magnitudes. Phase saturation of the two center-arm sums says each pair product has the phase of the center squared, which also aligns both cross sums. This gives precisely the listed affine phases and attains the bound. S=0 is trivial. Distinct lags in [-2,2]² remain distinct at independent orders N,M≥5, so the same formula/equality holds there without discretizing coefficient phases.
residual_risks: The independent finite check verifies the lag structure and attainment, not the global inequality by itself. The result does not classify aliased smaller grids.
